description:
My tech gear tends to get scuffed up as soon as I get them. Not on purpose, of course—it just happens as they’re carried around in my bag. The shiny new veneer that gives them their freshly minted look disappears all too quickly for my liking.

One example: The side of my headset got grazed almost immediately after I bought it, and I scratched a line on my smartwatch’s face by carrying it in the same sleeve as my laptop charger. Oops.

But there’s one piece of kit that hasn’t been tarnished: my gaming mouse. Why not? Because I got this $14 mouse carrying case at the same time and I’ve been using it from the get-go.
title: This $14 case is why my years-old gaming mouse still looks unboxed

description:
Mobile devices have become the primary way most of us browse the internet, making a reliable VPN for your phone more essential than ever. While plenty of VPN services cater to Windows users, a select few truly stand out on Android. I’ve narrowed down my favorites to help you find the best fit for your smartphones and tablets.

title: Best VPNs for Android: 5 top picks for phones and tablets

description:
You thought a Sophie’s Choice between ruinously expensive or embarrassingly underpowered laptops was as bad as the RAM crunch would get? Nope. It looks like we’re about to go backwards for graphics cards, too. A brand new AMD Radeon card has just been announced and… oof. Some variants appearing in pre-built PCs will start with just 4GB of GDDR6 memory.

AMD has officially announced the Radeon RX 9050 after a day or so of leaks and, if you look on the official spec page, it says that the Navi 44-based card (a shared platform with the 9060 and 9060 XT) has a “Max Memory Size” of 8GB.
title: Get ready for the return of 4GB graphics cards

title: Claude chats showed up in Google Search. Here’s how to keep yours private

description:
On July 23rd, several Microsoft services (Azure, Windows Update, and Microsoft 365 apps like Teams and SharePoint) experienced widespread outages, which blocked the installation of Windows 11 updates. This delay was all the more frustrating because Microsoft now explicitly says to install Windows updates ASAP for security reasons.

Microsoft is now working on a number of fixes for Windows Update, which will hopefully reduce the risk of future problems.

Windows Update Orchestrator and Arbiter

According to Neowin
title: A Microsoft outage blocked Windows updates. Now a fix is being tested

description:
The hottest company on the planet right now is a memory supplier called CXMT, a name barely anyone outside of China had even heard a year ago. It’s making headlines in financial markets on a massive stock debut, predicated on the idea that it’s going to fill the hole in the DRAM market (the kind of memory that goes into consumer PCs) as the big three make bank on “AI.”

Well bully for CXMT (ChangXin Memory Technologies), I suppose. This is, undeniably, good news if you’re looking for DRAM in mainland China. But while the Chinese market often affects technology across the world, it can also be insular, changing only itself — a potential customer base of 1.4 billion people can occupy even the biggest mega-corps, after all. So my question in this week’s newsletter is, will the rise of CXMT actually lower memory prices for the broader market, and pot
title: China’s RAM boom is here. Your cheap PC is not
